summary: Feed s153_double is degraded: 23.2% duplicate packets and 44.0% one-way TCP sessions prevent IDS from reassembling flows and detecting attacks reliably.

findings.root_cause: Same packets delivered twice via overlapping SPAN/TAP feeds aggregated to the same tool port without broker deduplication - broker is forwarding both sides of the link or duplicate SPAN copies.
findings.impact_on_tool: IDS wastes ~23% of capacity processing duplicates, inflates counts, causes state confusion and false positives, and risks missing real attacks due to resource exhaustion.

recommended_fix.why: Enable packet broker deduplication to drop identical packets within a short window before delivery, restoring accurate traffic volume and freeing IDS capacity for real detection.

findings.root_cause: Only one direction of TCP sessions reaches the IDS - likely asymmetric routing, single-direction SPAN (Tx-only), or broker load-balancing splitting client/server directions to different tool ports without flow-aware aggregation.
findings.impact_on_tool: IDS needs_both_directions=true for TCP reassembly and signature matching; with 51 of 116 sessions (44%) one-way, it cannot reconstruct flows and will miss exploits, C2, and exfiltration.

recommended_fix.why: Configure packet broker to aggregate both directions of each flow to the same IDS port using 5-tuple flow-aware hashing, ensuring complete bidirectional sessions for detection.
